title: Vampire shoppers
reason: 从科技与 AI 轮换到金融消费与数字生活。节目讨论深夜网购、疲劳判断和冲动控制，既贴近日常消费，也能迁移到金融科技中的行为风险与产品设计。练习围绕六个高频表达反复调用，从原文支撑的回忆逐步过渡到改写、受限工作场景应用和有限自由表达。

objectiveQuestions.prompt: What does 'get sucked into something' mean in the discussion of late-night shopping?

options.text: Become involved and find it hard to stop.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: The transcript defines the expression as being unable to stop yourself getting involved in something you did not intend to do.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the transcript-based expression: Parents, shift-workers and gamers may shop late when they are ______.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Why can tired people make poor shopping decisions at night?

options.text: They cannot use payment systems after midnight.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Rob says that when people are very tired, they do not always think straight and can make bad decisions.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: Complete the expression: Sleep deprivation can make it harder to ______ to spend.
objectiveQuestions.explanation: Helen Undy explains that lack of sleep reduces people's ability to control spending impulses and resist the urge to spend.

options.text: A legal right to a refund.

objectiveQuestions.explanation: Neil explains that a feel-good factor is something that gives a person a happy and positive feeling.

objectiveQuestions.prompt: How can lack of sleep and mental-health problems affect spending, according to Helen Undy?

Use this structure: (1) topic - what vampire shopping is and who may do it; (2) two key ideas - how tiredness affects judgement and spending control, and why a purchase may feel good at first; (3) conclusion or example - regret, returns or one way to avoid an impulsive purchase. referencePoints: Vampire shopping means shopping online late at night, when many other people are asleep.
Sleep-deprived parents, shift-workers, gamers and people with insomnia may be awake and tempted to shop.
Because online shops are open all day, tired people can get sucked into shopping and may not think straight.
Sleep deprivation and mental-health problems can reduce control over spending impulses and make advertising harder to resist.
Buying something can provide comfort or a short feel-good factor, but shoppers may later regret the purchase.
Research mentioned in the programme found that many people did not return the last online purchase they regretted.
